subject: science
title: Clapping Hands Make Sound
objective: Describe how clapping hands make sound and how to use sound safely.
introduction: Milo claps his hands and hears a sound. What vibrates, and how can Maxine listen safely?

A vibration that travels through air or another material to your ears.

items.prompt: Maxine claps her hands. What starts the sound she hears?
items.explanation: Clapping makes the hands move and vibrate, and that vibration starts the sound. Lamps, blankets, and cars are not the cause here.

items.prompt: Milo is near very loud music. Which action is safest for his hearing?

options.text: Cover his ears and move away

items.explanation: Very loud music can hurt ears, so covering them and moving away reduces the sound reaching them.

items.prompt: Milo reads four claims about sound. Which one is NOT true?

options.text: Sound travels through perfect empty space

items.explanation: Sound needs matter such as air to carry vibrations, so it cannot travel through a perfect vacuum. Claps and drums vibrate to make sound.

items.prompt: Maxine claps and feels a quick movement in her hands. Which example shows how sound begins?
items.explanation: Clapping makes the hands vibrate, and that vibration makes sound. Lamps, windows, and mirrors describe light rather than the sound source.

items.prompt: Milo listens to music at home. Which action helps protect his hearing?

options.text: Press a speaker next to an ear
Listen for hours without a break

items.explanation: Lower volume is gentler on ears, and breaks also help protect hearing. Very loud or close sound can cause harm.
